data.body:
PRE-IMPLEMENTATION VERIFICATION OF THE PROBE CRITERIA (AC5 / AC6). All three premises CONFIRMED in
the tree at df41edcf25, independently of the session that wrote the plan. These are the two hardest
ACs and both rest on claims that would silently produce vacuous pins if wrong, so they were checked
rather than trusted.

1. THE _backend() SEAM GENUINELY CANNOT SEE THE PROBE CLASSIFIER. Confirmed:
   tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py FakeTransport.probe_remote returns
   'ProbeResult(branch=ProbeBranch.UNREACHABLE, issue_key=remote_id, detail={})' UNCONDITIONALLY —
   no branch logic at all. Its own comment explains it returns a real ProbeResult rather than None
   so a delegation assertion cannot pass with an unusable value; it is a delegation stub, not a
   classifier. So AC5's prohibition is correct: pins written through
   JiraDataCenterBackend(transport=FakeTransport()) would assert this static return and could NEVER
   reach PRESENT_RESOLVED, PRESENT_FILTERED or ARCHIVED_OR_MOVED.

2. THE DC BACKEND MERELY DELEGATES. Confirmed at
   adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py: 'def probe_remote(self, remote_id): return
   self.transport.probe_remote(remote_id)' — one line, no classification. So the real behaviour is
   only reachable via jira_family.classify_probe_response or a JiraDataCenterTransport over a
   jira.JIRA-shaped stub, exactly as AC5 says.

3. THE VACUITY HAZARD IN AC6 IS REAL, NOT THEORETICAL. Confirmed byte-identical:
       adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:37
           DEFAULT_RESOLVED_STATUSES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"})
       adapters/jira/probe.py:39
           RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = frozenset({"Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"})
   Same three members. So at defaults the two sets are INDISTINGUISHABLE and any pin claiming 'DC
   binds its own resolved_statuses' would pass identically against Cloud's constant — a test that
   cannot fail, which is precisely what sibling story 2944 exists to delete. AC6's requirement to
   pass a NON-DEFAULT set (e.g. frozenset({"Custom Resolved"})) and assert the cross-set
   discriminator is therefore load-bearing, not belt-and-braces. An implementer who 'simplifies' it
   to the defaults reintroduces the defect this epic is about.

IMPLEMENTER NOTE: the four branches must come from the classifier, and the discriminator must come
from a custom set. Those are two separate requirements and satisfying the first does not satisfy the
second.
